meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екундочка'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'one little second, a moment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Wait, just now, one little second.
Just a second, I'll be right back!
Yes, of course. Wait, just now, one little second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'call; bell' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.
examples.trans: General Kruglov is waiting for a call. If you'd be so kind.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'брасывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reject a call, drop'.

related.gloss: to to reject a call (prefixed perfective)
not to to reject a call (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Why do you keep hanging up on my calls?
Yet she hangs up on me for the second time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'этому').

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.
I'm tired, so I'm at home.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'званивать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call back'.

related.gloss: not to to call back (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: That is why I am calling you back.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет перезванивать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to call back without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from; of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'man' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.
This man is waiting for you.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'висеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to depend on'.

related.gloss: not to to depend on (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Но всё зависит только от вас.
examples.trans: But everything depends only on you.

examples.text: Соберись, экономика города зависит от тебя.
examples.trans: Pull yourself together, the city economy depends on you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'низительно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь, что это унизительно?
examples.trans: Don't you understand that this is humiliating?

examples.text: А быть безработным — это не унизительно?
examples.trans: And being unemployed — isn't that humiliating?

examples.text: Нина, ты не понимаешь, что это унизительно?
examples.trans: Nina, don't you understand that this is humiliating?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy; occupied, taken').

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ступить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start, get down to'.

examples.trans: Forgive me, let us get started.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет приступить без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to start without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'множко'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to work a little.

examples.text: Мне нужно немножко поработать с бывшим мэром.
examples.trans: I need to do a little work on the former mayor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корректировать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to adjust, correct'.

examples.text: Мы бы хотели немножко скорректировать меню.
examples.trans: We would like to make a few adjustments to the menu.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет скорректировать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to adjust without a reason.

meanings.note: Indeclinable neuter noun borrowed from French 'menu' (detailed list, from Latin 'minutus').

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?
examples.trans: What's this menu here? How do I make a call?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
